fields.meta_description: Build a vendor application for your market or festival that scores booth photos and checks permits. Every applicant lands in a table you own.
fields.h1: Build a Vendor Application That Fills Booths and Checks Permits
fields.hero_description: Describe your market, your booths and what each vendor must send. Emergent builds the vendor application and sorts every applicant into a booth or the waitlist.
fields.features_heading: What a Vendor Application Should Handle
fields.features_subheading: A PDF collects a name and a booth size. These six pieces turn it into a vendor list a market manager can run on.
fields.feature_1:
Product categories that fill and close

Set how many stalls each category gets, such as 3 for bread or 6 for produce. Once a category fills, new applicants in it go to a waitlist in the order they applied.
fields.feature_2:
Photo uploads scored by your jurors

Ask each maker for photos of their work and their booth setup. Jurors open one application at a time and score it out of 5. The app adds up every score and ranks the pool.
fields.feature_3:
Permits read for their expiration dates

Food vendors upload a health permit and an insurance certificate. The app reads the dates off each document and asks for a new one when it runs out before the event.
fields.feature_4:
Supplier registration with a W-9

Purchasing offices collect a W-9 and a list of what each business supplies. Each registration waits for a buyer to approve it, and only approved suppliers can get orders.
fields.feature_5:
Booth offers and reminders by email

Send each accepted vendor a booth offer with the load-in time and stall number. Anyone who has not confirmed gets a reminder, and an unclaimed booth goes to the waitlist.
fields.feature_6:
Your code, on your GitHub

Export the full codebase to GitHub when the application grows into a vendor portal with logins and stall maps. A developer can host it on your servers and keep adding to it.
fields.why_title: Why Build Vendor Applications With Emergent?
fields.why_description: Booths sell out early and permits expire. An application that checks both before the offer goes out saves the morning of the event.

fields.tab_content_1:
Bread caps at three stalls, waitlist after

Cedar Hollow sells bread at 3 stalls each Saturday and no more. When Rye and Rise applied as the fourth baker, its application went to the bread waitlist instead of the manager's inbox. Produce still had 2 of its 6 stalls open, and the farm that applied that morning got a booth offer by email.
fields.tab_content_2:
12 of 15 from the jurors earns a booth offer

Three jurors score every applicant's photos out of 5 each, since Juniper Street gets more makers than booths for its holiday market. Any maker whose total reaches 12 of a possible 15 gets a booth offer by email. Applications below that line wait until the jury finishes the whole pool, in case booths are left.
fields.tab_content_3:
Is the insurance still good on festival day?

Food trucks applying to Harbor Lights upload a county health permit and a certificate of insurance. The app reads each expiration date and checks it against July 18, festival day. Smoke Point BBQ's certificate ran out June 30. The owner got an email asking for a renewed copy, and the booth offer stayed on hold.
fields.tab_content_4:
Purchasing approves each supplier in Slack

Maple Grove buys road salt and plumbing repairs only from businesses that register first. Its vendor registration form asks for a W-9 and the goods or services the business sells. Each registration posts to the purchasing channel in Slack, where a buyer approves it before the supplier can receive a purchase order.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Vendor Application
fields.howto_description: Settle what you are selling space for and who decides before you open the builder.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Decide who the application is for
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 List what you will sell space for
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Ask for photos that show the booth
fields.howto_step_1_des: A vendor application either fills booths at an event or registers suppliers who want to sell to your organization. Markets and fairs ask about products and booth needs. Purchasing offices ask for tax details and the goods or services each supplier offers.
fields.howto_step_2_des: List every booth size and how many of each you have, such as twelve 10x10 spaces and four corner spots. Then cap each product category. A market with 3 bread stalls says so on the form, and applicants past the cap join a waitlist.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Ask for photos of the products and one of a past booth setup, since jurors judge both. Name the file types you accept and a size limit. For food vendors, add the permit and insurance certificate your health department and venue require.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Agree on how jurors score and what total earns a booth. One score out of 5 per juror is enough for most fairs. Write the reply for applicants below the line, and decide whether they wait for leftover booths or hear no right away.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Paste your booth caps and scoring rule into one prompt. Emergent builds the vendor application with a database of applicants behind it and a review screen for jurors. Ask in plain English when you want to change a cap or a deadline later.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Connect your email for booth offers and reminders, and Slack for the jury or purchasing channel. Each new application then reaches the people who decide without anyone checking a spreadsheet. Accepted vendors get the load-in time and their stall number in one message.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Run one fake applicant through the form before you share the link. Apply in a category that is already full and upload an expired certificate. Then check that the waitlist entry and the request for a new certificate both arrived where you expect them.
fields.hero_prompt: Build a vendor application for my farmers market with stall caps per product category, booth photos and a waitlist.

claims_to_source: Form W-9 is how a business gives a requester its correct taxpayer identification number
Florida businesses that sell taxable goods register with the Florida Department of Revenue to collect sales tax before they start selling
South Carolina sellers of goods at retail need a retail license from the SC Department of Revenue
Vendors who want to sell to the State of South Carolina register for a state vendor number through the state procurement office
A sole proprietor does not need to register a business entity such as an LLC with the state
Food vendors at a temporary event need a temporary food establishment permit from the local health department, applied for before the event
